title: Cybersecurity's Next Phase: Competing Business Models in a Growing Market
author: Ilaria Sangalli
description:
July highlighted the growing divergence within the technology sector. While the Nasdaq-100® (NDX®) and the S&P Technology Select Sector Index declined 6.6% and 8.0%, respectively, broader equity markets proved more resilient, with the MSCI World Index gaining 0.5% and the S&P 500 ending the month roughly flat. Against this backdrop, the ISE Cyber Security UCITS™ Index (HUR™) declined 1.8% during the month, demonstrating relative resilience compared with broader technology benchmarks. 

The relative resilience of cybersecurity stocks suggests investors continue to view security spending as a strategic priority rather than a discretionary expense. Importantly, AI adoption appears to be creating additional demand for cybersecurity solutions rather than displacing existing security budgets, as organizations seek to protect AI models, sensitive data and increasingly complex digital environments. As a result, cybersecurity is emerging as a key beneficiary of the broader AI investment cycle. Recent comments from IBM support this view, indicating that enterprise customers continue to prioritize cybersecurity spending even as they accelerate investments in AI.
